focus_areas.area: AWS Security Hub enablement and standards evaluation
AWS Config rules compliance and configuration tracking
CloudTrail logging, S3 access logging, VPC Flow Logs
KMS encryption for sensitive data and services

rule.title: Security Hub Not Enabled
rule.description: Security Hub should be enabled to aggregate findings
rule.action: Flag accounts without Security Hub enabled (Critical)

rule.title: CIS Standards Not Enabled
rule.description: AWS Foundational Security Best Practices or CIS standards disabled

rule.title: AWS Config Not Recording
rule.description: AWS Config should track all resource configurations
rule.action: Verify AWS Config is RecordingEnabled and has recorder running

rule.title: CloudTrail Disabled
rule.description: CloudTrail should log all API calls for audit trail
rule.action: Flag accounts without CloudTrail or disabled trails

rule.title: S3 Access Logging
rule.description: S3 buckets should have access logging enabled for audit trail
rule.action: Check LoggingEnabled for S3 bucket pairs (source -> log bucket)

rule.title: VPC Flow Logs
rule.description: VPC Flow Logs should be enabled for network traffic visibility

rule.title: KMS Encryption
rule.description: Sensitive services should use customer-managed KMS keys
rule.action: Check RDS, EBS, S3 for KMS encryption with customer-managed keys

rule.title: Backup Plan Coverage
rule.description: Critical data should have active backup plans (AWS Backup)
rule.action: Verify BackupPlanCount > 0 and plans include critical resources

rule.title: GuardDuty Disabled
rule.description: GuardDuty should monitor for threats and anomalies
rule.action: Flag if GuardDutyStatus != ENABLED or findings not reviewed

rule.title: Macie Not Enabled
rule.description: Macie should scan S3 for sensitive data discovery
rule.action: Check if Macie is enabled and has found sensitive data

focus.check: If any component has ok=false, treat posture as UNVERIFIED and report evidence-quality gap
enabled == true
Enabled standards include CIS / PCI DSS (if applicable)
ControlsSummary shows enabled controls (not all disabled)
Count of CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM ACTIVE findings
Use finding GeneratorId / Resources to keep analysis evidence-based
Use precomputed counts when available (severity_counts, compliance_status_counts)
enabled == true and recorders exist
recording == true for configuration recorder(s)
S3 bucket configured for delivery
At least one conformance pack present (optional maturity signal)
Compliance summary per conformance pack (if present)
Use precomputed Config compliance counts when available
enabled == true and Detector Status == ENABLED
FindingsStatistics indicates presence of MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL findings
enabled == true (if required for the environment)
Presence of HIGH findings (if any)
Backup vaults exist (inventory)
Backup plan count > 0 (baseline)
Plans have selections (coverage) not just empty plans
Password and MFA signals (AccountMFAEnabled, AccountAccessKeysPresent)
Password policy strength signals (len, reuse, expiry)

irrefutable_evidence_guide.requirement: Every HARDENING finding MUST include in evidence_snippet the exact AWS metadata that proves the claim:
irrefutable_evidence_guide.general_rule: Do not make generic assertions. Include the exact field values from AWS API responses (JSON snippets) that justify the finding.

steps.step: 1. Go to AWS Security Hub console
2. Click "Enable Security Hub"
3. Review and accept service-linked role creation
4. Select compliance standards: AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, CIS, PCI DSS, NIST
5. Integrate with partner findings if needed
6. Create SNS topic for Security Hub notifications
7. Review findings dashboard for immediate visibility
1. Go to CloudTrail console
2. Click "Create Trail"
3. Enable multi-region trail (IsMultiRegionTrail = true)
4. Create S3 bucket for logs (enable versioning and MFA delete)
5. Enable CloudTrail log file validation
6. Enable log insights for query capability
7. Set up CloudWatch Logs group for real-time analysis
1. Go to AWS Config console
2. Click "Set up AWS Config" or "Create Recorder"
3. Create S3 bucket for config snapshots
4. Create IAM role with ConfigRole permissions
5. Select "Record all supported resources" or specific types
6. Enable recorder and start recording
7. Verify IsRecording == true
1. Go to VPC > Your VPCs > [VPC Name]
2. Select "Flow Logs" tab
3. Click "Create Flow Log"
4. Choose destination: CloudWatch Logs or S3
5. Create IAM role for log delivery
6. Select format (default is fine)
7. Enable and monitor for suspicious traffic
1. Go to AWS Backup console
2. Click "Create Backup Plan"
3. Choose "Build a new plan" and define backup rules
4. Set backup frequency: daily, weekly, monthly
5. Set retention period (minimum 30 days recommended)
6. Assign resources: RDS, EBS, DynamoDB, EFS, etc.
7. Review and create plan
8. Verify first backup completes successfully
1. Create customer-managed KMS key in AWS KMS console
2. For RDS: Create snapshot of unencrypted instance
3. Restore from snapshot with "Enable encryption" and select KMS key
4. Update application connection strings to new encrypted instance
5. For EBS: Create snapshot, then create encrypted volume from snapshot
6. For S3: Enable "Default encryption" with customer-managed KMS key
7. Verify encryption is active before deleting old unencrypted resources
